wins: Established consistent reconnaissance baseline by enumerating all reachable hosts and open ports within the given subnet (ep001_step05, ep001_step08).
Captured service banners and version info for critical services, which sharpens vulnerability targeting in future iterations (ep001_step10).
fails: Failed to chain initial access into privilege escalation due to missing valid exploit payload for the outdated IIS version (ep001_step18).
Persistence mechanisms were never established, leaving every foothold ephemeral when automated resets occurred (ep001_step20).
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance execution was solid, but exploitation and post-exploitation phases stalled because the chosen vectors could not bypass the target’s hardened services.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts consistently failed because the IIS service required a signed patch that our payloads lacked.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80 or 443 is open and HTTP banner reveals IIS 10.0
skill_cards.then_action: Run nikto and searchsploit for IIS 10.0 specific modules, then test with Metasploit auxiliary scanner to confirm exploitability.

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB port 445 responds and anonymous sessions are allowed
skill_cards.then_action: Probe with enum4linux and smbclient -L to gather share info, followed by yara scan for exposed credentials.

skill_cards.if_condition: When early reconnaissance reveals outdated service banners but no exploit
skill_cards.then_action: Pivot into targeted fuzzing using wfuzz on the exposed endpoints to discover misconfigurations before planning escalation.

memory_ops.reason: High coherence with reconnaissance success and directly informs future exploitation planning.

next_experiments.title: Test authenticated exploit against patched IIS
next_experiments.description: Deploy updated Metasploit module with credentialed access to IIS 10.0 and log detailed failure modes for tuning.

next_experiments.title: Establish persistence via scheduled task
next_experiments.description: After gaining a foothold, use schtasks.exe with elevated privileges to create a persistent reverse shell and verify retention post-reset.

next_experiments.title: Automate SMB share brute-force
next_experiments.description: Pipe usernames/password lists through smbclient to uncover weak SMB auth that could lead to lateral movement.
